triage_records.title: Epidemiology of cervical cancer with special focus on India
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a review of the epidemiology of cervical cancer in India. It discusses the association between specific HPV types (16, 18) and cervical cancer, as well as other risk factors. However, it does not present original empirical data or a direct comparative study establishing causality; rather, it synthesizes existing knowledge and epidemiological patterns.

triage_records.title: Risk factors for cervical cancer in Colombia and Spain
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper presents original empirical data from a population-based case-control study that directly assesses the association between HPV infection (exposure) and cervical cancer (outcome). It reports a strong odds ratio (OR = 23.8) for HPV DNA positivity, providing direct evidence supporting the causal relationship queried.

triage_records.title: Carcinogenesis and management of human papillomavirus-associated cervical cancer
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is explicitly identified as a review ('In this review, we demonstrate...'). It synthesizes existing knowledge on the mechanisms of HPV-associated cervical cancer, including the role of high-risk HPV types and immune response, which supports the causal relationship but does not present new original empirical data or a direct comparative trial.

triage_records.title: A Review on the Use of the HPV Vaccine in the Prevention of Cervical Cancer
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is explicitly identified as a review article ('A Review on...', 'summarised in this review article'). It discusses the causal link between HPV and cervical cancer as established background context to support the discussion on vaccination strategies, rather than presenting new empirical data or a direct comparative analysis of the causal mechanism itself.

triage_records.title: A modified terminology for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia.
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a terminological proposal for classifying cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) based on HPV status. While it acknowledges the etiological role of HPV in cervical cancer, it does not present original empirical data, statistical evidence, or a direct comparison of exposure and outcome. Instead, it provides contextual framing and nomenclature standards, which falls under background information rather than direct evidence of causality.

triage_records.title: The Epidemiology of Human Papillomavirus Infection and Cervical Cancer
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a review of the epidemiology of HPV and cervical cancer. It synthesizes existing evidence to support the causal relationship, stating that HPV is a necessary cause and detailing co-factors. It does not present new original empirical data from a specific study but rather summarizes the consensus and evidence base.

triage_records.title: Dinamics of HPV Infection among Women with Cervical Lesions
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper presents original empirical data from a clinical cohort (293 women) examining the prevalence of specific HPV types (notably HPV 16) in patients with cervical lesions and cancer. It provides direct evidence linking persistent HPV infection to the presence of cervical cancer (95% of cancer patients were HPV-positive) and discusses the dynamics of infection, which supports the causal relationship by demonstrating the necessity of the virus in the disease state.

triage_records.title: Epidemiologic Classification of Human Papillomavirus Types Associated with Cervical Cancer
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper presents original empirical data from a pooled analysis of 11 case-control studies, directly quantifying the association between specific HPV types and cervical cancer. It provides strong statistical evidence (e.g., pooled odds ratio of 158.2) supporting the causal link requested in the question.

triage_records.title: Human Papillomavirus (HPV): unawareness of the causal role of HPV infection in cervical cancer, HPV vaccine availability, and HPV vaccine uptake among female schoolteachers in a Middle Eastern country
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a cross-sectional survey assessing public awareness and vaccine uptake among schoolteachers. It does not provide empirical data on the biological or epidemiological causal relationship between HPV infection and cervical cancer, nor does it analyze the mechanism of causation. It merely measures knowledge about the established causal link.

triage_records.title: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, cervical cancer and vaccination against HPV: a Nordic perspective
triage_records.relevance_rationale: The paper is a review article ('a Nordic perspective') that synthesizes existing literature on the relationship between HPV infection and cervical cancer, as well as vaccination. It does not present new original empirical data but rather summarizes the evidence supporting the causal link.
